title: New Mexico businesses share financial impact of federal tariffs with state lawmakers - NewsBreak
text:
By Jordan Honeycutt No media credit provided. ,
54 minutes ago
NEW MEXICO (KRQE) – New Mexico lawmakers are learning more about how President Donald Trump’s tariffs are impacting local businesses. Three businesses told the Federal Funding Stabilization Subcommittee this week that the tariffs are hitting them hard. The leader of a copper business said about half of the copper used in the U.S. is imported since what’s made domestically can’t keep up with demand. Since tariffs went into effect, they say domestic copper companies have raised prices 10% to 20% due to a lack of competition, making it tough to stay afloat.
Food banks in New Mexico prep for increase in need with projected pause of SNAP amid shutdown One lawmaker noted how this could impact local construction. “When we’re bidding these big projects, including projects like Project Jupiter, and you need a transformer that needs copper and these other things, what does that really do to construction costs? At the end of the day, it goes through the ceiling,” said Rep. Patricia Lundstrom (D-McKinley County).
When a state lawmaker asked what they could do to help, the businesses said to keep advocating for them when communicating with the federal government.
